meta.title: Hawky — know when Claude Code is waiting for you
meta.description: A Mac menu bar app that tells you when Claude Code is waiting for permission or for your next prompt, and takes you to that tab in one click. Works with Cursor and VS Code.

hero.tagline: Claude Code is waiting. Hawky noticed.
hero.lead: Run Claude Code in a few repositories at once and one of them will stop and wait — silently, in a window you are not looking at. Hawky keeps watch from the menu bar and takes you straight to that tab.

steps.title: A session stops
steps.body: Claude Code waits for your permission, or for your next prompt.

steps.title: The count shows up
steps.body: The number of permission waits appears next to the hawk, with the number of working sessions and a small spinner beside it. Nothing pops up to interrupt you.

steps.title: One click takes you there
steps.body: The session's tab comes to the front. ⌃⌥H does it too.

title_match.title: Finds the right tab
title_match.body: However many windows and tabs share a repository, Hawky tells them apart by the session's title.

tabs.title: Looks behind macOS tabs
tabs.body: Merged your windows into macOS tabs? Hawky still finds the tab behind them.

clears.title: Clears itself
clears.body: Approve, deny or type your next prompt and it goes away. Close the editor and anything left goes too.

finished.title: Shows who is waiting for a prompt
finished.body: A session that has finished and is waiting for your next prompt is listed on its own, without adding to the count.

working.title: Counts working sessions too
working.body: The number of sessions Claude Code is working on sits under the permission count, with a small spinner. A session you stop with Esc drops out of it.

install.title: Setting it up

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Hawky into Applications, or use Homebrew.

steps.title: Let it open
steps.body: The author is not a registered Apple developer, so the first launch is blocked. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

steps.title: Connect it to Claude Code
steps.body: Choose Settings… in Hawky's menu and click Connect.

install.accessibility: Allow Accessibility access when Hawky asks. It uses it to bring the tab to the front.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Hawky notices when Claude Code is waiting and brings the right tab to the front. That's the whole app. It has no server, no analytics, and no account.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.body: Hawky's Claude Code hook writes a small file for each session that is working, or waiting for permission or for your next prompt: the session ID, the folder it was opened in, the session title from the end of its transcript, where the transcript is, the ID of its Claude Code process, the app it runs in, and the time. The app reads those files, and the titles of Cursor's and VS Code's windows and tabs so it can find the right one. For a working session, it reads the end of the transcript to tell whether you stopped it with Esc, looking only for the note Claude Code leaves when that happens. It does not otherwise read your code or your conversations.

sections.title: Nothing leaves the Mac
sections.body: Those files live in ~/.claude/hawky/pending and are deleted when the session's Claude Code process ends. Nothing is collected or uploaded. There is nowhere for it to be uploaded to.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Hawky checks for a new version once when it starts, not on a timer. The check fetches a small file from its GitHub Releases page, so GitHub sees the request the way it sees any download, including your IP address. It carries nothing about your sessions.

sections.title: No analytics, ever
sections.body: There is no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no unique identifier, and no third-party SDK of any kind in the app.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Hawky is open source under the MIT license, so none of the above has to be taken on trust. Read the source, or open an issue if something looks wrong.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version starts doing something new with your data, this page gets updated before that version ships.
